candidates.name: Dermatomyositis
support_spans: Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Diffuse poikiloderma involving upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
Nailfold examination showed dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles
Radiographic evidence of myositis
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)
Presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms, including skin eruptions, muscle weakness, and specific laboratory and imaging findings, are consistent with dermatomyositis.

candidates.name: Juvenile Dermatomyositis
support_spans: A 14-year-old girl presented with a 6-year history of a photosensitive eruption
Her symptoms began at age 8 years
candidates.why: The patient's age and the duration of her symptoms suggest a diagnosis of juvenile dermatomyositis.

candidates.name: Autoimmune Disorder
support_spans: She had previously tried multiple medications including systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), with minimal improvement
candidates.why: The patient's lack of response to various immunosuppressive medications suggests an underlying autoimmune disorder.
